item.title: Gunmen kill two policemen, set station, operation van ablaze in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe Unknown gunmen have killed two policemen and burnt buildings and a patrol van at the Uratta Police Division, in Aba, Abia State. Confirming the incident, Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the Command, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed that the hoodlums attacked the division with explosives, resulting in a fire that damaged part of the building and the divisional patrol van. She added that two police officers lost their lives, while three inspectors sustained injuries and are currently receiving medical attention. The Command further clarified that no firearms or ammunition were carted away by the attackers during the incident. The PPRO explained that the Commissioner of Police, Abia State Command, CP Wilfred Afolabi, had personally led an operational team to the area. She also stated that the team combed the surrounding environment and restored calm, while intensified security operations and monitoring are ongoing to apprehend the hoodlums. The PPRO assured that the Command will deploy all necessary operational and intelligence resources to identify and apprehend those responsible, assuring that the hoodlums will be brought to justice. “The Command extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of the fallen officers and the entire Police family over this painful loss. “Residents are urged to remain calm, vigilant and to support the Police with credible information that could assist the ongoing investigation. “Information can be reported at the nearest police station, through the suggestion boxes and contact details of the DPO’s provided at police divisions, or via the Command’s emergency hotlines: 08035415405,08079210004, 08079210005, 08079210006.” Vanguard gathered that Governor Alex Otti had visited the police station as well as the injured policemen at the hospital. item.title: Nigeria awaits 10 attack helicopters, UAVs — Defence Minister
item.description: EU pledges €20m defence support to Nigerian military By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Nigeria is expecting the delivery of 10 attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other military equipment to strengthen its capacity to tackle emerging security threats, the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), has said. Musa disclosed this when he received the European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, and his delegation at Ship House, Abuja. The meeting focused on bilateral defence agreements, including a review of security cooperation between Nigeria and the EU, as well as a proposed €20 million assistance package for the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the European Peace Facility. In a statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, Special Assistant on Media to the Minister, Mignot commended Nigeria’s defence leadership and invited Musa to a meeting of defence ministers in Brussels later in the year. The minister said the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, on which more than 50 million people depend, remained a potential source of instability. He added that denying terrorists access to their strongholds on islands in Lake Chad remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). Musa thanked the EU for its continued support for Nigeria and assured the ambassador of President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to protecting lives and property and promoting national development. He said relative peace was gradually returning to parts of the country through the efforts of the Armed Forces and other security agencies. However, he acknowledged that kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities persisted, adding that security agencies were working to address the threats. On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme, the minister stressed that its implementation should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel. Mignot disclosed that an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details for delivering the proposed assistance. He also commended a recent conference of former and serving MNJTF force commanders, which was attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission. item.title: PSG fight back to beat Strasbourg after Dembele penalty miss
item.description: Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty but later scored as Paris Saint-Germain produced a fightback to win 3-1 away at Strasbourg on Saturday and go to the top of the French Ligue 1 table. PSG were trailing to an early goal by United States star Giovanni Reyna for Strasbourg at the Stade de la Meinau, and last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembele then put a penalty wide in the 72nd minute. But Dembele made amends in style, first by setting up Illia Zabarnyi to equalise in the 78th minute and then by putting the reigning French and European champions ahead with five minutes to go. He then played a part in setting up Desire Doue for PSG’s third in stoppage time, as Luis Enrique’s men made it four straight Ligue 1 wins, and six on the bounce including the Champions League. After failing to win any of their first three domestic league matches this season, PSG are up to 14 points from seven games and are therefore top of the standings on goals scored from Monaco, before the principality club visit Lorient on Sunday. Lille, Rennes, Paris FC and Lyon all have the opportunity to go back above PSG in the table over the weekend. This game, one of PSG’s toughest domestic tests of the season, fell awkwardly just three days after their 4-2 Champions League victory at Manchester City and three days before they host Barcelona. True to form, Luis Enrique therefore made sweeping changes with eight in total from the City game. Dembele was one of those relegated to the bench here with an eye on the upcoming meeting with Barcelona, his former side. Strasbourg sought to take advantage and went in front on 17 minutes when Reyna received a Gessime Yassine pass just inside the area, turned and beat Matvey Safonov low at the goalkeeper’s near post. The visitors were grateful to Safonov for a superb save low down to deny Conrad Harder just after half-time, before Luis Enrique sent on some of the cavalry, including Dembele and Doue. They won a penalty after a VAR check confirmed that a Doue shot had hit the arm of Pape Demba Diop, but Dembele — who scored a penalty in May’s Champions League final win over Arsenal — put his spot-kick wide. However, Dembele crossed from the right for Ukraine defender Zabarnyi to equalise with a cushioned close-range finish, and then controlled on the edge of the box before firing in to make it 2-1. That was his first Ligue 1 goal this season to go with three in the Champions League, and Dembele — who is nominated again for this year’s Ballon d’Or — then brought down a long Safonov kick before finding Ferran Torres who set up Doue to seal the win. Lille are looking to bounce back from a 3-0 Champions League loss at Arsenal when they entertain Brest later, knowing a win will take them to the summit. item.title: Remi Tinubu urges more opportunities for vulnerable families
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — First Lady Oluremi Tinubu has called for sustained efforts to expand access to education, healthcare, skills acquisition, decent livelihoods and economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable families, as Nigeria joins the world to mark the 2026 International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. In a message issued on Saturday, Tinubu said the occasion, observed under the theme “United for Peace and Human Rights,” highlighted the collective responsibility to build a society where everyone could live with dignity and hope. “The International Day for the Eradication of Poverty 2026, with the theme ‘United for Peace and Human Rights,’ reminds us of our collective responsibility to build a society where every person can live with dignity and hope, access meaningful opportunities, and thrive to realise their full potential,” she said. The First Lady stressed that efforts to tackle poverty must prioritise vulnerable households and create conditions that enable people to improve their living standards. “We must continue expanding access to education, healthcare, skills, decent livelihoods, and economic opportunities, especially for vulnerable families,” she said. She added that compassion, effective interventions and sustained collaboration were essential to helping individuals and families escape poverty. “Through compassion, effective interventions, and sustained collaboration, we can create pathways out of poverty and towards shared prosperity,” she said. Tinubu wished Nigerians a happy International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. The day is observed annually on October 17. According to the United Nations, the theme for 2026–2028 is “United for Peace and Human Rights”, while the focus for this year is “Safe Homes for All”. item.title: Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu. Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers. He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse. He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office. “Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said. He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians. item.title: Troops rescue 27 abducted residents in Katsina Forest
item.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina KATSINA — Troops of the Nigerian Army, working with local hunters and the Community Watch Corps, have rescued 27 residents abducted by armed bandits during an attack on Gamji village in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State. The attack, which occurred on Friday, also claimed the life of a 70-year-old resident, Alhaji Saleh Kasim, while six cows were reportedly rustled. The Katsina State Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026. According to the statement, signed by the state Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr Nasir Mu’azu, about 40 armed bandits, reportedly led by a gang leader identified as Kachalla Alhaji Bawa Kabir, invaded the community in the early hours of October 16 on 20 motorcycles. The attackers abducted 27 residents, comprising mainly women, children and elderly people, and killed Kasim during the raid. The ministry said security forces launched a coordinated operation after receiving intelligence about the attack. Troops of the 17 Brigade mobilised alongside local hunters and members of the Community Watch Corps to pursue the fleeing attackers and secure the release of the victims. The joint security team reportedly blocked escape routes towards the Madaci forest enclave to prevent the bandits from moving the abducted residents deeper into the forest. The operation culminated at about 6pm on Friday when troops engaged the suspected bandits at Tashar Bawa forest and rescued all 27 victims, according to the statement. The rescued residents were subsequently taken to the Machika Military Forward Operating Base for medical attention and other necessary care. The ministry added that joint security teams had commenced clearance operations to track down suspected members of the gang who escaped the encounter. The operations are also aimed at preventing possible reprisal attacks and protecting Gamji and neighbouring communities from further threats. Mu’azu commended the troops of the 17 Brigade, local hunters and the Community Watch Corps for their prompt response, courage and cooperation, which he said contributed to the successful rescue. He reaffirmed the commitment of the Katsina State Government, under Governor Dikko Umaru Radda, to protecting lives and property and intensifying security operations in communities affected by criminal activities. He added that worsening inflation had increased the burden on ordinary Nigerians, arguing that the country’s arable land, water resources and human capital should enable it to tackle hunger and malnutrition through coordinated action. Ginger production crisis Speaking at the event, a food safety advocate, Dr. Shego, raised concerns about the decline in Nigeria’s ginger production, alleging that contaminated agricultural inputs contributed to a devastating outbreak of ginger blight disease that destroyed farmers’ harvests. He recalled that Nigeria was previously among the world’s leading ginger exporters but suffered severe production losses that increased its reliance on imported ginger. According to him, farmers who used certain agricultural inputs supplied under intervention programmes began noticing black spots, blight and softening in their crops before harvest. The National Assembly has also rejected existing ad hoc arrangements of personnel training which, according to it, are not sustainable and lack the institutional capacity the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies ( NILDS) is known for. item.title: Scientists name newly-discovered plant species after Messi
item.description: Scientists have named a newly identified plant species in Peru after Argentine football star Lionel Messi, with the species classified as endangered. The plant, named Salvia messii, is found in the Andes mountains of central and southern Peru, where climate change and forest fires threaten its survival. According to The Athletic, the plant’s light blue and white flowers resemble the colours of Argentina’s national team jersey. The discovery was documented in a study published in the October 2026 edition of the scientific journal Phytotaxa, titled “A remarkable new Salvia (Lamiaceae) from the ecotonal vegetation surrounding the western Andean relict forests of Peru”. The plant belongs to the mint family and can grow to about 1.5 metres tall. It thrives on rocky, dry mountain slopes at elevations between 2,000 and 2,400 metres above sea level. The research was led by Paúl Gonzáles of the Natural History Museum of the National University of San Marcos, alongside Argentinian researcher Rolando Uría and biologist Jean Capcha Ramos of Huarango Nature. The name Salvia messii follows botanical naming conventions, which use the suffix “i” to indicate that a species is named in honour of a person. item.title: Ogun hospital probes nursing student’s death amid negligence allegations
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The management of the Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Aro, Abeokuta, Ogun State, has launched an investigation into the death of a Post-Basic Nursing student, Taiwo Godwin, following allegations of medical negligence in the treatment of an asthma attack. The hospital management, in a statement issued on Saturday, expressed sadness over Godwin’s death, which occurred while he was receiving treatment at its General Medical Practice Unit. The investigation follows reports alleging that the deceased developed breathing difficulties while playing football and was subsequently rushed to the hospital for medical attention. A source, said to be a colleague of the deceased, alleged that Godwin was still able to walk into the hospital’s emergency unit upon arrival, but later suffered a deterioration in his condition. The eyewitness reportedly accused the medical personnel on duty of failing to administer oxygen to the student despite his worsening condition. The source further alleged that although oxygen equipment had been placed on the patient, the oxygen supply was not switched on. The eyewitness also claimed that the medical team encountered difficulties while attempting to gain intravenous access and secure the patient’s airway. Reacting to the incident, the hospital management assured students, staff members and the general public that a thorough investigation was underway to determine what transpired. The statement, signed by the hospital’s Public Relations Officer, Mr Abiola Ajibola, on behalf of the Acting Provost and Medical Director, said the investigation would be conducted in accordance with established procedures. The management also pledged to expedite the process and ensure that it was thorough, impartial and transparent. “We further assure all concerned that every necessary step will be taken to establish the facts, address any issues identified, and ensure that justice is served,” the statement said. The hospital further promised to cooperate with relevant authorities and stakeholders as required, while appealing to members of the public to exercise restraint and allow the investigation to run its course. “While we appreciate the concerns and emotions surrounding this tragic event, we urge the public to remain calm and allow the investigation to proceed without prejudice to its findings,” the statement added. The management reiterated its commitment to patient safety, professional accountability and the maintenance of the highest standards of medical care within the institution. It also expressed condolences to Godwin’s family, friends, colleagues, fellow students and members of the nursing community over the loss. item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The management of the Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Aro, Abeokuta, Ogun State, has launched an investigation into the death of a Post-Basic Nursing student, Taiwo Godwin, following allegations of medical negligence in the treatment of an asthma attack. The hospital management, in a statement issued on Saturday, expressed sadness over Godwin’s death, which occurred while he was receiving treatment at its General Medical Practice Unit. The investigation follows reports alleging that the deceased developed breathing difficulties while playing football and was subsequently rushed to the hospital for medical attention. A source, said to be a colleague of the deceased, alleged that Godwin was still able to walk into the hospital’s emergency unit upon arrival, but later suffered a deterioration in his condition. The eyewitness reportedly accused the medical personnel on duty of failing to administer oxygen to the student despite his worsening condition. The source further alleged that although oxygen equipment had been placed on the patient, the oxygen supply was not switched on. The eyewitness also claimed that the medical team encountered difficulties while attempting to gain intravenous access and secure the patient’s airway. Reacting to the incident, the hospital management assured students, staff members and the general public that a thorough investigation was underway to determine what transpired. The statement, signed by the hospital’s Public Relations Officer, Mr Abiola Ajibola, on behalf of the Acting Provost and Medical Director, said the investigation would be conducted in accordance with established procedures. The management also pledged to expedite the process and ensure that it was thorough, impartial and transparent. “We further assure all concerned that every necessary step will be taken to establish the facts, address any issues identified, and ensure that justice is served,” the statement said. The hospital further promised to cooperate with relevant authorities and stakeholders as required, while appealing to members of the public to exercise restraint and allow the investigation to run its course. “While we appreciate the concerns and emotions surrounding this tragic event, we urge the public to remain calm and allow the investigation to proceed without prejudice to its findings,” the statement added. The management reiterated its commitment to patient safety, professional accountability and the maintenance of the highest standards of medical care within the institution. It also expressed condolences to Godwin’s family, friends, colleagues, fellow students and members of the nursing community over the loss. item.title: COAS tasks troops on enabling environment for free, fair elections
item.description: The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lt Gen Waidi Shaibu, has urged troops of the Nigerian Army to ensure a secure environment for the conduct of free, fair and credible elections in the country. Shaibu gave the charge on Saturday in Maiduguri while addressing troops during a routine visit to the Headquarters of the Joint Task Force, North-East, Operation HADIN KAI, at Maimalari Cantonment. He said much was expected from the troops in the discharge of their constitutional responsibilities, particularly in safeguarding the nation’s territorial integrity and supporting democratic processes. The army chief spoke after a closed-door meeting with commanders and heads of formations in the North-East theatre. He emphasised the need for professionalism, discipline and dedication among personnel, urging them to remain committed to their duties. Shaibu said the visit was also aimed at assessing the welfare and operational readiness of the troops deployed to combat insurgency in the region. He expressed satisfaction with their morale, noting that the personnel remained in high spirits and determined to defend the country. The COAS urged the troops to sustain their commitment to duty and conduct themselves professionally while carrying out assigned tasks. He reaffirmed the Nigerian Army’s commitment to protecting Nigeria’s territorial integrity and supporting efforts to maintain peace and security. Shaibu’s visit formed part of ongoing engagements with field commanders and personnel to assess operational activities and reinforce military effectiveness in the North-East. item.title: Oborevwori to leaders: Politics must not come before God
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has warned political leaders against allowing political engagements to undermine their commitment to God, insisting that playing politics and serving God are two distinct responsibilities. Oborevwori spoke in Abuja on Saturday after receiving the Christian Icon Award from the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) at the National Christian Centre during the association’s 50th anniversary celebration. “We may be involved in politics, but we must be able to distinguish between serving God and playing politics. These are two different responsibilities, and we must never allow politics to undermine our commitment to God,” Oborevwori said. The governor expressed gratitude to God for the honour, describing it as a call to greater service to humanity. “My faith and commitment to serving the people and humanity remain strong. It is a great honour to be recognised, particularly by the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN). “When an organisation such as CAN gives you an award, it means a lot because the recognition is based not merely on public service but also on integrity, character and the impact you have made,” he said. Oborevwori disclosed that his commitment to ushering work predated his emergence as Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, adding that he continued the practice despite advice to discontinue it because of his political position. He maintained that service to God and humanity required sincerity, dedication and a strong sense of responsibility, rather than the pursuit of personal pleasure or recognition. The governor also called for unity among Christian groups, expressing support for efforts to bring CAN’s five blocs together. “I commend the efforts to bring the five blocs together. If they remain united and speak with one voice, I believe they can contribute significantly to the development of the country. Their unity will strengthen the Christian community and, in turn, contribute to a more united Nigeria,” he said. Presenting the award, CAN President Archbishop Daniel Okoh said the honour was reserved for distinguished leaders whose political engagements reflected excellence, integrity, faith and commitment to nation-building. He added that Oborevwori’s contributions to national development continued to inspire generations. Those who accompanied the governor included his predecessor, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa; Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Emomotimi Guwor; members of the National Assembly, Victor Nwokolo, Nicholas Mutu and Jonathan Ukodhiko; Chief of Staff, Government House, Johnson Erijo; and Senior Political Adviser to the Governor, Senator Emmanuel Aguariavwodo, among other government functionaries and political leaders. item.title: Youngsters Beat Palace Chiefs 1-0 In Ewuare II 10th Coronation Anniversary Novelty Match
item.description: The Benin Palace playfield in Benin City came alive on Friday evening as youthful exuberance triumphed over experience in a high-stakes novelty football match held to commemorate the 10th coronation anniversary of His Royal Majesty, Omo N’ Oba N’ Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II. The match, one of the key events lined up for the historic anniversary, kicked off in royal splendor after Oba Ewuare II performed the ceremonial kick-off. It was a symbolic clash between wisdom and youth, as the Palace Chiefs took on the Royal Sceptre Bearers in a keenly contested encounter. The Sceptre Bearers, led by Senior Sceptre Bearer Frank Nomwengho, who thrilled spectators with mesmerising dribbling skills, dominated much of the play. Oba Ewuare II performed the ceremonial kick-off of the novelty football match held to commemorate his 10th coronation anniversary on October 17, 2026. The deadlock was broken early when 15-year-old winger, Aizenomwan Eboh fired the youngsters into the lead just six minutes into the game, sparking wild celebrations. Unfazed by the pace and energy of the young lads, the Chiefs, marshalled like the fortified walls of the ancient Benin Kingdom, stood firm and resisted relentless pressure. George Obasogie, a chief, led several attempts to find an equalizer, but the ironclad defence of the Sceptre Bearers held firm until the final whistle. The match ended 1-0 in favour of the Royal Sceptre Bearers. Among the dignitaries who witnessed the encounter in royal grandeur were the Benin monarch, his queens, members of the royal family, palace chiefs and functionaries, Edo State Football Association Chairman, Fred Erhunmwunse, and a large crowd of jubilant spectators. Speaking after the match, the coach of the winning side and retired FIFA-graded referee, Steven Amadin, praised his players for adhering strictly to instructions. Oba of Benin, Ewuare II (second-right, attends his 10th coronation anniversary novelty match at his palace in Benin City, Edo State, on October 16, 2026. He commended Oba Ewuare II for incorporating sports into the anniversary celebration. Also speaking, the Edo FA chairman described the novelty match as a fitting appetizer to the grand finale of the Oba Ewuare Cup. He lauded the monarch for using sports as a tool to foster unity and youth engagement. Adding traditional colour to the celebration was a thrilling traditional wrestling exhibition, Igba-Eze. Current national champion, Fred Osamudiamen, defeated 2018 All-Africa champion, Martins Amasin, to clinch the title, while Amasa Oko finished third. Presentation of rewards to winners and participants in the various sporting events will be held on November 21, 2026.
